Cognition: Sensory memory
Very brief storage of incoming sensory information
Working memory
Active manipulation of information held briefly in mind
Long-term potentiation
Strengthening of neural connections underlying learning
Encoding specificity
Recall improves when retrieval conditions match encoding conditions
Mnemonic device
A memory aid organising information for easier recall
Chunking
Grouping items into meaningful units to expand memory capacity
Spacing effect
Distributed practice producing better retention than cramming
Serial position effect
Better recall of items at the beginning and end of a list
Proactive interference
Old learning disrupting recall of new information
Retroactive interference
New learning disrupting recall of old information
Misinformation effect
Memory altered by misleading information encountered afterward
Availability heuristic
Judging likelihood by how easily examples come to mind
Representativeness heuristic
Judging by similarity to a prototype while ignoring base rates
Confirmation bias
Seeking evidence that supports what you already believe
Functional fixedness
Failing to see an object used in a novel way
Framing effect
How a question is worded changing the decision made
Algorithm
A step-by-step method guaranteed to reach a solution
Convergent thinking
Narrowing options to find a single correct answer
Development and Learning: Classical conditioning
Learning an association between two stimuli
Unconditioned response
An automatic reaction requiring no learning
Conditioned response
A learned reaction to a previously neutral stimulus
Generalization
Responding to stimuli similar to the conditioned one
Discrimination in learning
Responding only to the specific conditioned stimulus
Spontaneous recovery
A extinguished response reappearing after a rest period
Operant conditioning
Learning driven by the consequences of behaviour
Fixed-ratio schedule
Reinforcement after a set number of responses
Variable-ratio schedule
Reinforcement after an unpredictable number of responses, highly resistant to extinction
Shaping
Reinforcing closer and closer approximations of a target behaviour
Observational learning
Acquiring behaviour by watching a model
Schema
A mental framework organising and interpreting experience
Assimilation
Fitting new information into an existing schema
Accommodation
Revising a schema to fit new information
Object permanence
Knowing objects exist when out of sight
Conservation
Understanding quantity is unchanged by a change in shape
Secure attachment
A bond where a child explores freely and is soothed by the caregiver
Zone of proximal development
The gap between what a learner can do alone and with guidance
Social Psychology and Personality: Fundamental attribution error
Overweighting personality and underweighting situation when judging others
Self-serving bias
Crediting success to yourself and blaming failure on circumstances
Cognitive dissonance
Discomfort from conflicting beliefs that drives attitude change
Foot-in-the-door phenomenon
Agreeing to a small request making a larger one more likely
Conformity
Adjusting behaviour to match a group standard
Normative social influence
Conforming to be liked or accepted
Informational social influence
Conforming because you believe others know better
Obedience
Complying with the directives of an authority figure
Groupthink
Poor decisions caused by a group prioritising harmony over accuracy
Group polarization
Discussion pushing a group toward a more extreme shared position
Social facilitation
Improved performance on well-learned tasks when observed
Social loafing
Reduced individual effort when responsibility is shared
Bystander effect
Reduced helping when other people are present
In-group bias
Favouring members of one's own group
Just-world hypothesis
The belief that people generally get what they deserve
Big Five traits
Openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism
Reciprocal determinism
Behaviour, environment, and cognition continually influencing each other
Self-efficacy
Belief in your own capability to succeed at a specific task
Mental and Physical Health: Diathesis-stress model
Disorders arise when a predisposition meets environmental stress
Biopsychosocial model
Health explained by biological, psychological, and social factors together
Generalized anxiety disorder
Persistent uncontrollable worry not tied to a specific threat
Panic disorder
Recurrent unexpected surges of intense fear with physical symptoms
Obsessive-compulsive disorder
Intrusive thoughts paired with repetitive rituals
Post-traumatic stress disorder
Lingering distress, flashbacks, and hypervigilance after trauma
Major depressive disorder
Prolonged low mood and loss of interest that impairs functioning
Bipolar disorder
Alternating episodes of depression and mania
Schizophrenia
Disorder involving delusions, hallucinations, and disorganised thought
Positive symptoms
Added experiences such as hallucinations or delusions
Negative symptoms
Absent behaviours such as flat affect or withdrawal
Cognitive behavioral therapy
Treatment targeting unhelpful thoughts and behaviours together
Systematic desensitization
Pairing relaxation with gradual exposure to a feared stimulus
Token economy
A behavioural system reinforcing target behaviour with exchangeable tokens
SSRI
An antidepressant that increases available serotonin
General adaptation syndrome
Selye's alarm, resistance, and exhaustion response to stress
Learned helplessness
Passivity after repeated experience of uncontrollable events
Resilience
The capacity to adapt and recover after adversity
